howToRead.title: How to read a health indicator
howToRead.intro: Every indicator on a profile uses the same card. Here's what each part means.

example.title: Current asthma, adults
example.subtitle: Adults who were told by a health professional they have asthma and still have it

parts.title: What's measured.
parts.body: The indicator name and a plain-language description. Select "read more" for the full definition.

parts.title: This neighborhood's value.
parts.body: The most recent estimate for the community district you're viewing.

parts.title: Compared to NYC.
parts.body: How far above or below the citywide value it is. "Pts" means percentage points. The arrow and color show whether that's better or worse for health.

parts.title: Neighborhood, borough, city.
parts.body: The same measure shown three ways, so you can see the gap at a glance.

parts.title: Year and source.
parts.body: When the data was collected and where it comes from.

parts.title: Details.
parts.body: Opens a panel showing where this neighborhood ranks among all 59, plus notes about the data.

symbols.title: Interpret with caution.
symbols.body: The estimate is based on a small sample, so it is less precise.

symbols.title: Not shown.
symbols.body: There were too few responses to report a reliable estimate.

navigation.title: Switch neighborhoods
navigation.body: Use "Find neighborhood" to search by name or address. The whole profile updates to match.

navigation.title: Compare to another neighborhood
navigation.body: Pick a second neighborhood under "Compare to" to see both side by side on every card.

navigation.title: Jump to a topic
navigation.body: The topic menu takes you straight to a section, like chronic conditions or housing.

navigation.title: Search indicators
navigation.body: Search for any indicator by name and go straight to its card.

howToRead.tourPrompt: Want to see it on a real profile?

tour.replayHint: Need a refresher later? Open the ? menu and choose "Take the guided tour."
tour.endedToast: Tour closed. You can replay it anytime from the ? menu.

desktopSteps.title: Choose a neighborhood
desktopSteps.body: Search any of NYC's 59 community districts by name or address. Everything on the page updates to the place you pick.

desktopSteps.title: Compare two places
desktopSteps.body: Pick a second neighborhood here to see both side by side on every card.

desktopSteps.title: Start with At a Glance
desktopSteps.body: Key facts about who lives here, with comparisons to the city as a whole.

desktopSteps.title: Jump to a topic
desktopSteps.body: Use this menu to move between topics like chronic conditions or housing. The highlighted topic shows where you are on the page.

desktopSteps.title: Read an indicator
desktopSteps.body: Each card shows the neighborhood's value, how it compares to NYC, and when the data is from. The buttons on the card open more.

desktopSteps.title: Open Details
desktopSteps.body: Opens a side panel with more information about this indicator, plus a map.

desktopSteps.title: About this data
desktopSteps.body: The ? button explains how this measure is defined, where the data comes from, and anything to keep in mind when reading it.

desktopSteps.title: See the chart bigger
desktopSteps.body: Opens a larger version of the chart that you can save as an image, download as a spreadsheet, or embed on another site.

mobileSteps.title: Find your neighborhood
mobileSteps.body: Search by neighborhood name or address. The whole profile updates to match.

mobileSteps.title: Move between topics
mobileSteps.body: Open the topic menu at the top to switch topics, or use the "Continue to" button at the end of each one.

mobileSteps.title: Read an indicator
mobileSteps.body: Each card shows the neighborhood's value and how it compares to NYC.

mobileSteps.title: Get more on any indicator
mobileSteps.body: Tap Details for more information and a map. Tap ? to learn how the measure is defined and where the data comes from.
